newsitem.title: TURKEY: Car sales in Turkey rise 41 pct in Jan-July.
newsitem.headline: Car sales in Turkey rise 41 pct in Jan-July.

text.p: Passenger car sales in Turkey rose by 41 percent to 168,877 in January-July 1997 from the same 1996 period, with the market share of imported cars jumping to 33 percent from previous 20 percent, the Automotive Industry Association (OSD) said on Thursday.

It said sales of imported cars jumped by 131 percent to 55,772 units in the first seven months, compared to the same period in the previous year. Sales of locally produced cars rose by only 18 percent to 113,105 units.

Around 2,500 cars were imported in June and July, the first two months of a scheme whereby Turks could import vehicles at reduced duties after opening one-year foreign exchange accounts of at least 50,000 marks at government banks.
The OSD said Turkey's automotive industry exports fell by eight percent to $733.7 million in January-July this year from $797.2 million in the same 1996 period.
The biggest drop was in passenger car exports which dived 61 percent to $77.1 million and led to a 35 percent fall to $220.8 million in overall motor vehicle exports.
Automotive parts exports on the other hand, rose by 13 percent to $512.9 million in the seven-month period, compared to a year ago.
Turkish passenger car production fell three percent year-on-year in July to 21,523 units and was almost unchanged at 132,770 in the first seven months of 1997, compared to the same periods in 1996.
Turkey's overall motor vehicle output was up eight percent to 32,345 units in July and up nine percent to 212,823 in the first seven months of this year.
